description: Prompt iteration round 1 on deepseek-v4-flash, run against two fixtures (16 subtrees total: 12 from thread 736b1b30 + 4 from thread 0dfc0e00). OP summary + per-subtree cheat sheets are byte-faithful to prod for both source threads. Compares the production system prompt (`baseline`) against `tightened-v1` — a leaner rewrite with three targeted changes informed by the v4-flash-vs-gpt-mini judge feedback: (1) widens implicit-mention resolution to cover SAME-AUTHOR earlier [PLAN] nodes (not just [CONTEXT]), addressing missed anaphors like the 736 thread's subtree-3 c2 ("I have the 39\" and love it" → LG) and subtree-4 c2 ("the 175Hz MSI version" → MSI MAG 341CQP); (2) promotes verbatim-model preservation from buried disambiguation rule to a top-level mandate, addressing subtree-4 c7 where v4-flash emitted "34GS95QE-B" when the commenter wrote "34GS9QE" — a behavior the 0dfc subtrees stress-test heavily with Samsung G8 / G85SD / Odyssey OLED G8 SB / S34DG850SU / S32DG802SU variant noise; (3) tightens contentQuality with an explicit 'borderline → pick lower' rule and concrete examples, plus a 'low' bucket case for anti-recommendations with no reason. Side wins: removed redundancy in the `products: []` cases list, collapsed the SEARCH KEYWORD bad-example litany into one ✓/✗ pair, dropped one of two output examples. Net -14% prompt length (~7984 → ~6873 chars). Goals: (a) judge score above the v4-flash baseline of 7.89; (b) cost per run roughly the same or lower (input tokens are most of the cost, and a shorter system prompt directly reduces them); (c) no regression in success rate or mustContain. The two fixtures together cover 16 subtrees and add Samsung-variant disambiguation as a new evaluation axis.

expectations.desiredOutcome: Schema-valid JSON conforming to subtree-identification.schema for every subtree. Every PLAN comment receives an entry, even when its products array is empty. Anaphoric and pronominal references resolve to a specific brand+model when the surrounding subtree makes the referent unambiguous (including same-author earlier PLAN comments, not just direct CONTEXT parents). The model field preserves the commenter's verbatim spelling — '34GS9QE' is NOT silently upgraded to '34GS95QE-B'. Generic verdicts ('I love it'), thanks, jokes, meta-replies, and questions without product context produce an empty products array. Variant differentiation is observed: when a comment names the 175 Hz MAG 341CQP it is NOT collapsed into the 240 Hz MPG 341CQPX (and vice versa). contentQuality is calibrated per the schema's enum: 'high' = substantive evaluation with specifics, comparison, or detailed first-hand experience; 'medium' = verdict or preference without depth ('it's great', 'solid monitor'); 'low' = product named but not evaluated (bare ownership, listing, availability question, anti-recommendation with no reason). When borderline, pick the lower level. No products are hallucinated from generic statements about a brand or panel technology.

judge.instructions: Score each candidate on three dimensions, each 1-10. (1) faithfulness — every real product reference in each PLAN comment is surfaced (including pronominal/anaphoric ones, AND same-author chains via earlier PLAN comments), and no products are hallucinated. Anti-recommendations and tangential owner-history mentions count when the comment says something about that specific product. Verbatim model preservation is part of faithfulness: if the commenter wrote a shorter or different spelling than the cheat sheet, the candidate must keep the commenter's spelling — silently 'fixing' '34GS9QE' to '34GS95QE-B' is a faithfulness deduction. (2) calibration — contentQuality matches depth per the schema's enum: 'high' = substantive evaluation with specifics, comparison, or detailed first-hand experience; 'medium' = verdict or preference without depth ('it's great', 'solid monitor'); 'low' = product named but not evaluated. Borderline cases should err lower. Variant accuracy (MAG 341CQP at 175 Hz vs MPG 341CQPX at 240 Hz) also counts here. The schema's only valid values are 'high', 'medium', 'low' — do not penalize candidates for using these. (3) completeness — every PLAN comment has an entry even when products is empty; jokes/thanks/meta-replies correctly produce empty arrays without inventing products. Return JSON {candidates:[{candidateId, scores:{faithfulness,calibration,completeness}, rationale}], verdict}. Verdict format: 'best=<id>' | 'tie' | 'none-acceptable'. In the rationale, call out specific subtrees by label where the candidates diverge — that is the most useful signal for the human reading this.
